reason: The plant needs compressed carbon dioxide, and the receiver appears intended to collect it from the capture unit.
expectation: I expect the receiver to collect compressed carbon dioxide, though I don't know whether another preparation will be needed.

alternatives.reason: Starting water electrolysis also serves a stated goal, but I chose to prepare the carbon dioxide supply first.

effect: The capture unit supplied compressed carbon dioxide and completed that goal, leaving water separation as the next task.
reaction: It is satisfying that the plant can draw a useful ingredient from the thin atmosphere.
reason: Water electrolysis is the remaining stated goal, and the hydrogen outlet is one of two compatible ways to start.
expectation: I expect the electrolyzer to produce hydrogen from the water, though I am unsure how the oxygen will be handled.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen outlet also appears relevant to separating water, but I chose to start with hydrogen.

effect: The plant is running and has separated the hydrogen stream; the oxygen remains to be collected from the same process.
reaction: The explanation clarified why the same water appears at both outlets.
reason: Collecting oxygen is the only available combination and should complete the water-separation goal.
expectation: I expect to collect the oxygen produced by the running electrolyzer and complete the goal.

effect: Collecting oxygen completed the water-separation goal and clarified that the lander will use it as an oxidizer.
reaction: The distinction between oxygen and fuel was a useful clarification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Collecting hydrogen was most worthwhile because the explanation made clear that both outlets belong to the same electrolysis process.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting oxygen felt somewhat repetitive because it was the only available combination after collecting hydrogen.

surprise.text: I learned that the plant captures a chemical ingredient from the thin Martian atmosphere.

arbitrary.text: Neither outlet was clearly preferable at first, so choosing hydrogen before oxygen felt like an arbitrary ordering.

continue.text: Yes. The early return and the specimens make me curious about what the receiving lab will find, though this chapter's plant preparations involved few decisions.
